commentary_title: Lackluster week in the Suezmax market
commentary_summary: The Suezmax tonne-miles index declined for the third week, ending at 102.1 points. Meanwhile, there was an uptick in vessels at anchor MoM with a corresponding decline in vessels underway. | it was a quiet week for the Sezmax market as rates declined WoW. Tonnage demand towards the UKC was weak causing rates on WAF to UKC to decline further. | There were some trickle-down effects from the relatively firmer demand in the VLCC markets, supporting rates on ex-USG. | Freight rates are, however, likely to weaken further in week 37 due to waning tonnage demand in the VLCC segment.
